brief: livingAt() names every duck, swan, dog and person under the pointer, but birds are named only on the near roof. A pigeon on the courtyard lawn, on the lane, or standing on the plaza roundel — where #92 gave them their own roll and cap precisely so they would be there — answers nothing at all when you point at it. That is the one visible hole in the town's naming, and it is on the most-used offer after #where. Close it: every bird the town draws should say what it is and, where the town knows, where it is. People & animals is eight iterations back and has had exactly one interaction vector in the whole run.
successLooksLike: Pointing at a bird anywhere in the town names it, at every camera position and on a phone tap, and the naming survives the bird hopping or flying while the pointer is still on it.
avoid: Do not add a new entry to OFFERS[] — this is the existing touch offer doing its job, and a second offer waits 19.5 real seconds behind the queue. Keep the hit test on the same predicate everything else uses; do not give birds their own parallel path.
